issues.legal_issue: A tenancy confined to land does not constitute accommodation where tenant-built structures never became the landlord’s property.
material_facts: The land was originally let to a tenant who built a verandah and a room on it.
The original tenant did not return possession of the land and structures to the landlord, but transferred them to the appellant.
The courts found that the structures never became the landlord’s property and that the appellant’s tenancy from the landlord was for the land alone.
The landlord’s successors filed an ejectment suit without obtaining permission from the District Magistrate.
issues.conclusion: The land alone did not fall within the statutory definition of accommodation, so permission from the District Magistrate was not required before filing the ejectment suit.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 2(a) of the U.P. (Temporary) Control of Rent and Eviction Act, 1947, accommodation means residential or non-residential accommodation in a building or part of a building. Section 3 requires the District Magistrate’s permission for a suit to evict a tenant from accommodation. Where the tenancy is only of land and tenant-built structures never became the landlord’s property, the tenancy is not of accommodation for these purposes. Section 108(h) of the Transfer of Property Act permits a lessee to remove constructions made by the lessee while still in possession. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.ejectment_suit: A landlord or successor sought to recover possession of rented property through an ejectment suit.
predicates.tenancy_was_only_for_land: The tenant’s tenancy from the landlord covered land alone, rather than a building or part of a building.
predicates.tenant_built_structures_never_became_lan: The tenant-built structures did not become the landlord’s property before the tenant transferred possession of the land and structures.

issues.definition: When an ejectment suit concerns a tenancy only of land and the tenant-built structures never became the landlord’s property, the suit is not barred for lack of eviction permission.

issues.legal_issue: A lessor’s mere knowledge and inaction concerning tenant-made constructions do not estop the lessor from seeking ejectment absent conduct by the lessor that induced detrimental change.
material_facts: The appellant made constructions on the land, and the landlord knew about them but did not expressly consent to them.
The courts found no action by the landlord that caused the appellant to alter his position to his detriment.
The appellant relied on a description of the property in an allotment order, but that description was not a representation made by the landlord and was not shown to create rights supporting estoppel.
The appellant could remove the constructions while in possession.
issues.conclusion: The landlord’s mere inaction did not estop the landlord’s successors from bringing the ejectment suit, and the lease could be determined despite the constructions.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 108(h) of the Transfer of Property Act, a lessee may remove constructions made by the lessee while in possession. Section 111 does not bar a lessor from determining the lease merely because the lessee made constructions, even with the lessor’s knowledge. Mere inaction, without conduct by the lessor causing detrimental alteration of position, does not support estoppel; a description in an allotment order is not a representation by the lessor absent evidence that it created relevant rights. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: ejectment_suit and tenant_made_constructions and lessor_knew_of_constructions and lessor_did_not_induce_detrimental_change and allotment_description_was_not_lessor_representation and tenant_could_remove_constructions_while_in_possession

predicates.ejectment_suit: A lessor or successor sought to recover possession from a tenant through an ejectment suit.
predicates.tenant_made_constructions: The tenant made constructions on the rented property.
predicates.lessor_knew_of_constructions: The lessor knew that the tenant had made the constructions.
predicates.lessor_did_not_induce_detrimental_change: The lessor did not take action that caused the tenant to alter the tenant’s position to the tenant’s detriment.
predicates.allotment_description_was_not_lessor_rep: A description of the property in an allotment order was not a representation made by the lessor and was not shown to create relevant rights.
predicates.tenant_could_remove_constructions_while_: The tenant was entitled to remove the tenant-made constructions while still in possession.

issues.definition: When a tenant made constructions, the lessor knew of them but did not induce detrimental change, an allotment description was not the lessor’s representation, and the tenant could remove the constructions while in possession, the lessor is not estopped from seeking ejectment.
